fixes.explanation: A sign is a fair guess, baker. But the text says the elders are gathered to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from Zion, the City of David (2 Chronicles 5:2). It's the ark, not a sign.

Not quite, friend, and here's what the text says. When all the elders of Israel had arrived, the Levites took up the ark (2 Chronicles 5:4). Solomon, Israel's king, is the one who assembled the elders (2 Chronicles 5:2), but the Levites are the ones who take up the ark.

You got it, baker. The text says that when all the elders of Israel had arrived, the Levites took up the ark (2 Chronicles 5:4). Solomon, Israel's king, is the one who assembled the elders (2 Chronicles 5:2), but the Levites are the ones who take it up.
That's right, baker. The text says there was nothing in the ark except the two tablets that Moses had placed in it at Horeb (2 Chronicles 5:10). Nothing else was in there, just the two tablets.
Nice try, friend, but no robes in there. The text says there was nothing in the ark except the two tablets that Moses had placed in it at Horeb (2 Chronicles 5:10). Only the tablets were in it.
Goliath's sword is a big guess, baker. The text says there was nothing in the ark except the two tablets that Moses had placed in it at Horeb (2 Chronicles 5:10). Only the tablets are in there.
You got it, friend. The trumpeters and singers joined together to praise and thank the LORD with one voice (2 Chronicles 5:13). Trumpets, cymbals and singers, all praising together.

Good thought, since the text mentions singers and trumpeters. But it says they joined together to praise and thank the LORD with one voice (2 Chronicles 5:13). So they're praising together, not as two separate groups.

Turns would be polite, baker, but that's not what the text says. It says the trumpeters and singers joined together to praise and thank the LORD with one voice (2 Chronicles 5:13). They're together, not taking turns.
That's right, baker. The singers and trumpeters praise the LORD, and the temple, the house of the LORD, was filled with a cloud (2 Chronicles 5:13). Stay in your seat for this one.
